title: Leafcutter Ants Carry Leaves They Never Eat for 50 Million Years
subject: leafcutter ant

scenes.text: These ants carry leaves all day and never eat a single bite.
They feed the leaves to a fungus. The fungus is their only food.
They've farmed it for about fifty million years, long before humans invented farming.
They weed it, groom its spores, and keep antibiotic bacteria to fight off pests.
One abandoned nest was cast in cement: nineteen hundred and twenty chambers.
Two hundred and thirty-eight held fungus gardens. The farm covered sixty-seven square metres.

description:
Leafcutter ants never eat the leaves they carry. They feed them to a fungus, their only food, a partnership about 50 million years old.
A record nest cast in cement had 1,920 chambers, 238 of them fungus gardens, covering more than 67 square metres.
If ants can farm, what else are they hiding? Tell us below.
first_comment: A new queen carries a starter piece of fungus in her mouth to begin a new farm. Would you trust an ant with your garden?
